text_fidelity_a:
NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Break Open 15 Premium Geodes - With Goggles, Detailed Learning Guide, 3 Display Stands, Great STEM Science Toy & Educational Gift I recently received this geode kit. I was eager to bring it to a young friend of mine, a ten year old boy with an eye for science and a curious mind. The package and its photo of a young girl smashing rocks open promises at least a mild adventure, and what young man doesn't enjoy carte blanche to hit things with a hammer?

While my youthful pal did have a good time, I can chalk that more up to a willing sense of adventure than to the kit itself. First, a small gripe. The package depicts a little girl giving the rock her level best with a hammer and wearing safety goggles in the process. No hammer is included, but that's reasonable enough. (If you don't have a hammer, most likely geodes are low on your list of priorities.)

Still, the product seems designed as a dangerous source of fun for latchkey children, as only a single pair of safety goggles are included. Unless NatGeo assumes adults are down with little shards of rock storming their aqua vitreous, they really should have included a second pair. Unlike a hammer, I don't think safety goggles are a household staple.

The bigger issue with the product is the difficulty level in cracking the geodes. A giant Ziploc bag of small-to-medium size rocks is included, as well as some of the trinket-iest "display tables" I've ever seen, pieces of plastic that look to be pilfered from a Playmobil t-ball set. That's beside the point, though. Unless your child is sneaking steroids, these geodes are going to prove a most formidable foe. I cracked and whacked with all my (decent, adult) might and we only managed to get a couple open. If we had kept at it, we surely would have ended up with cartoonishly large dominant arms.

So it is good exercise, and hitting things with a hammer is usually a solid albeit not entirely safe source of fun for a kid. It would be disingenuous to say we had a bad time, but I can't give the product any real recommendation, either. If you do check it out, or get it as a gift, invest in that second pair of safety goggles to avoid giving your eyeballs that hipstery studded look, and don't let any kid hit these rocks by their lonesome if you value their fingers.
text_fidelity_b: NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Break Open 15 Premium Geodes - With Goggles, Detailed Learning Guide, 3 Display Stands, Great STEM Science Toy & Educational Gift

Power Wheels Jurassic Park Jeep Wrangler Ride-On Battery Powered Vehicle With Dinosaur Sounds & Lights For Preschool Kids Ages 3+ Years Power Wheels were pretty basic when I was a kid. They're so much more decorative and interesting nowadays! (Wow, that makes me sound old!) This little PW Jeep was easy to assemble, without any confusion or difficulty, and though the sticker additions are tedious, it's not hard & they peel off to restick if you mess up a little

So after assembling and decorating, there's battery charging. Your best option is to wait until the kiddos are sleeping to build and charge this. Or even better, do it at the grandparent's house! It takes quite a while to recharge, too, so I suggest purchasing a second battery to keep the fun going.

This is a fairly rigid frame that will protect the littles from any low-speed collisions. The specs say that this will hold 2 kids, aged 3-7, up to 130 lbs. I doubt you can fit two 75 lb 7-year-olds in this little Jeep, or you might need a pry bar to get them out! Maybe a couple 5-year-olds could fit ok. Mainly tall kids will have trouble getting into it. It's great for two preschoolers, though.

The two main fun features of this PW Jeep are the real lights on the "rollbar" and the dinosaur and chase sounds from the 'radio'! The awesome parental feature is the ability to set a slow speed for littles and increase to 5 mph as they learn better control. I also love the power-lock breaks that will stop this instantly if a little one steps on the pedal!

Loads of fun for the little raptor hunter!
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Jurassic Park Jeep Wrangler Ride-On Battery Powered Vehicle With Dinosaur Sounds & Lights For Preschool Kids Ages 3+ Years

I got this expecting to get some cool robots that would likely be invited over to tea with Barbie, but what I did not expect was how great these would look assembled. These robots have intricate touches on their armor that look really unique, and often hide the tell-tale Lego look that many of their creations have. The result is that these look more like real toys than something we put together.

There are a few minor quibbles. This comes with a lot of rare or unique pieces, but unlike a lot of kits, I have difficulty imagining using many of them beyond the specific applications of putting these kits together. A lot of very intricate and small pieces make these work. In addition, one of the figures slots into their robot perfectly, while the other is just tossed into a slot to rattle around, which feels pretty unfinished. A decidedly non-professional touch to a kit that would otherwise be worthy of display.

Overall though, a great character kit from Lego.

Scientific Explorer Geo Smash Mining My children have enjoyed various kinds of dig kits in the past, so they were excited for this one, too. My 5 year old got this one, and he liked it pretty well.

On my side, though, this particular kit wasn't one of my favorites. The kit comes with a hammer, but that thing was absolutely useless! My child was frustrated with it, so I gave it a try. Useless! The description tells you that you'll get a pair of goggles, but you don't. There's no goggles in this kit, but the instructions recommend that your child wear a pair. Also, I dislike that all of the rocks were clumped in one little spot in ours, and that happen to be right where my child started digging. He got them all dug out very quickly, but still had a great deal of clay to dig through. Discovering "treasures" slowly(at least more slowly than this one) is the whole fun of these things.

Like all dig kits, this one is messy. We've found shallow pie pans to be the best holders. The sides aren't too tall, so it won't hurt your child's arms. It also keeps the mess inside the pan. For the kits that are harder to dig, it makes it super easy to move the dig until your child wants to work on it again. This particular dig is on the softer side, though not the softest we've ever done. Really, it's just right in that area, for our tastes. It's not so hard that it's frustrating, but not so soft that the dig ends in a few minutes(or it wouldn't have if ours had the gems spaced out better).

Overall, if your child enjoys rocks(or gems), this is a decent choice. There are better options, though.
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Geo Smash Mining

Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike Coming from a family of mostly boys and Big Wheel lovers, I know these current low riding Big Wheels are not the same quality as my little brother's Big Wheel from 1971. My brother loved his Big Wheel so much, that my son also had to have one when he was 3. Even though he was too small, he didn't care- walking it was just as good as riding it.

Things haven't changed much in the design, the big wheel bikes are all still too large for children under 4-5, but the quality has changed a lot for the original Big Wheel. After replacing the back seat 3 times, the original current Big Wheel of our nephew's recently went to the garbage. Replacing the Big Wheel with a tricycle was even worse- after a couple turns- the head injuries even with a helmet proved to be going from a cheap big wheel to bruises.

This Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is very similar to the Big Wheel of the seventies- very sturdy. The seat doesn't break at the pegs like the current Big Wheel. It is still too large for children under 5, but they don't care- they enjoy just having it, even if they have to walk it. They use their feet anyway for braking, so they don't mind walking it until their feet reach the pedals. My son walked his Big Wheel for a year before he could reach the pedals.

The best thing about this Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is our nephews love it. Taking the fastest high speed turns ends up in falls inches from the ground- meaning less painful minor injuries. My brother and son never had a bad injury being so close to the ground and this was in the days of no head protection. Putting it together was not difficult with the directions and once together, it's hard to keep the kids off. It's nice to see Radio Flyer keeping the tradition of making a sturdy Big Flyer that is perfect for 4 to 7 year olds, just like in the seventies when things were built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike

Melissa & Doug Children’s Book - Soft Shapes: Ocean (Foam First Puzzle Book) This is an ingenious first book. It is like a puzzle book. The four puzzle pieces ~ a blue whale, a sea turtle, an octopus, and a seahorse ~ can be removed from the book and played with.

They even go into the bathtub and will float or stick to the sides.

This book is for four months on up. It is not intended for teething.

The colors are vibrant: blue greens, oranges and purples primarily. The ocean animals look cute and friendly.

The text is riddles in the form of who am I? It is rhyming although some of the rhyming is a tad clumsy, but your one or two-year-old won't care.

Here's a sample ~ see if you can guess who it is:

I have eight arms and two large eyes
And really am quite smart
I have no bones and squirt out ink
So predators depart.

The book uses big vocabulary words, but that's good for children to hear. As a former preschool director, kindergarten teacher and principal, I believe in exposing children to big concepts and expand their sense of the world past their everyday experiences. It grows their minds.

This is a gift for our one-year-old for Christmas - it makes for an original gift.

It does say: "Both additives may dissolve and damage the inks in this book." Not sure what additives they are talking about - bathing and teething? It says discard the toy if damaged. That should be made clearer.

4.5 stars
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Children’s Book - Soft Shapes: Ocean (Foam First Puzzle Book)

VIAHART Patrick The Pygmy Goat - 18 Inch Large Stuffed Animal Plush - by Tiger Tale Toys Oh, what have I done?

I bought Patrick the Pygmy Goat as a gift for my goat loving wife this past Christmas. Upon seeing it Christmas morning, her eyes lit up and she took to it immediately. I thought I had made the perfect choice.

Or so I thought.

I quickly found that it seems Patrick was always watching me. At night, he would sit atop the pillows on the bed watching over his new domain. Despite the fact his head seems to be affixed to only look to his left, it still seems he is looking at me no matter what side of the bed I’m on. When I tuck in my wife at night, he is there staring. When I come back from brushing my teeth, he is there staring. When I lift the sheets to turn over at night, he is there staring into my soul.

I’m pretty sure he is plotting against me. I can see him in the window looking down at me when I take the trash out to the street. I get phone calls with the sounds of capra aegagrus hircus breathing on the other end. Sometimes he is there under my feet when walking by or sitting on my chest when I wake.

I’ve spoken to my wife about my concerns, but she laughs them off. I’m starting to think she is in on it with the goat. With Patrick. Even now, he is watching me type.

Despite the above concerns, he appears to be a really great stuffed goat. My wife falls asleep with him in her arms each night as he whispers, whatever it is he is saying, into her ear.
text_fidelity_b: VIAHART Patrick The Pygmy Goat - 18 Inch Large Stuffed Animal Plush - by Tiger Tale Toys

text_fidelity_a:
JOY FOR ALL - Freckled Pup - Brown and White Soft-Touch Coat - Realistic and Lifelike Interactive Companion Pets A few years ago I purchased a similar “robo pet” (a cat) for my elderly Mom. It was cute and somewhat entertaining, but the motions were jerky and robotic, and the audio was rather poor. I was looking forward to trying this dog version out since I thought the tech would have improved over the past few years.

Sadly, no. The motions are still rather jerky and accompanied with a lot of mechanical noise. The range of motions exhibited is quite limited. The audio is of poor quality – it sounds like it is coming from a ten cent speaker. It performs about the same as the robo cat I purchased a few years ago for less then half the cost of this puppy. Given the price point, the performance was pretty disappointing.

On the plus side, the overall build quality shows some good attention to detail. The tongue and foot pads are rubbery plastic with a much nicer feel than you would expect. The fur is very well attached. On the downside, the fur feels fake and artificial.

This is not what I would call a “cuddly” pet due to the artificial fur feel plus the fact that it is pretty hard under the fur.

It runs on 4 C batteries, which come already installed. The battery compartment has a three position switch: on, off and mute. It is a little challenging finding the battery compartment – you have to really hunt for a seam on the underside which comes apart via Velcro.

Most of the feedback from the puppy is cute – it moves its head and barks/cries/pants when you scratch its ears. It also responds to sound so you can talk to it. The only routine it has that I didn’t care for is the heart beat. If you scratch its back, you’ll hear a heart sound. To be frank, I found that rather creepy – it sounded like something out of the Tell-tale Heart. On the plus side, once the heart sound was heard, the pup got the name Edgar.

While there have been some incremental improvements in the tech for these “robo pets” over the past few years, it’s still pretty crude. It might hold some fun for a small child, but the non-cuddly nature of it makes it a poor substitute for a plush animal that can be hugged (even if it doesn’t bark or cry). Two stars, since the performance does not come close to justifying the cost.
text_fidelity_b: JOY FOR ALL - Freckled Pup - Brown and White Soft-Touch Coat - Realistic and Lifelike Interactive Companion Pets

Sesame Street Playskool Discover ABCs with Elmo Playset This toy is pretty neat.

There's not much as far as assembly goes. (Just snapping 3 pieces together, and then attaching the whole building into that.) It only took a minute or so.

Elmo is detached from the rest of the set, and he holds onto a hand "lens". Letters are hidden throughout the building, on both sides. You can tell where a letter is going to be...circle with squiggly lines. You can't tell what letter it is until Elmo's "lens" is held over it, though. To find some of the letters, the child will have to turn a couple of wheels, and lift the trash can lid, but most of them are in plain view.

This is a fun little toy for learning letters. It doesn't take up a ton of room, either. It's somewhat flat in design, so it could easily slide into a little nook somewhere, and just pull it out for learning time. I think most children will tire quickly of it if they have full access to it, unless they have other Sesame Street toys(or something else similar) that could be used with it, apart from just hunting for letters. I think it's probably better for special times, though, for most children. There's really not a great deal to it, but it is fun and neat.

text_fidelity_a:
Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition Ok, I have to start this review off by saying I had my reservations about this game. I absolutely love Euro strategy games like Puerto Rico, Agricola, Power Grid, Caylus, etc, but I'm not into card games. In fact, I pretty much hate card games.

This game was getting a lot of publicity on BoardGameGeek and everyone was raving about it so I decided that I should buy it to give it a shot. I'm glad I did.

The whole point of the game is to build your deck of cards and build up a collection of victory points. The reason this game shines is because it is a quick game that only takes about 30-40 minutes to play. It is also very fun because as you are building your deck of cards you aren't usually getting rid of the cards. If you spend some gold to buy a card that gold goes back into your discard pile and will eventually be shuffled for you to use again in another turn.

There are over 500 cards in this game with around 25 different action cards available so you can vary the game a lot depending on what cards are currently on the table. The only downside is that someone that has played the game a lot and knows a base strategy can usually beat a new player easily.

Overall this game is very addicting and short, which is a good thing. You can play multiple rounds of this game in an evening as opposed to one game of another typical Euro.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition

text_fidelity_a: Perplexus Rookie (Styles and Colors Vary) My 8 year old daughter received the Perplexus for Christmas, and our whole family fought over it for the rest of the holiday break.  My youngest turned four in early January, so I immediately ordered the Rookie version for him.  It arrived quickly, as we've become accustomed to when shopping Amazon, so ordering on December 27th for a January 2nd party was not a problem. It's been in my son's grubby little paws for five days  now and he is enamored of the thing.  It's wonderful to see my very large, very rough and tumble four year old boy carefully, slowly, cautiously navigate this little ball bearing around the maze.  He twist it, turns it, lifts it so he can see it from the bottom, and growls when the ball falls off the track.  But then he gets right back to it.  He has beaten it, but that doesn't seem to diminish his interest in trying again.  Whoever came up with this idea for this toy has my respect.  I only gave it four stars for durability because it seems like it could be a little higher quality.  For such an amazing toy, the materials should be of a high enough quality to make it an heirloom.  It is honestly one of my favorite toys, along with quadrilla and magnatiles, so I wish it was a little more substantial.  We have had no problems with it as of yet, though, after five days of heavy use.

It’s a good physical outlet that is not only fun but promotes a multitude of skill building…. Color recognition, sizing and comparison (tall/short, large/small), balancing. text_fidelity_a:
KLUTZ Make Your Own Mini Erasers Toy includes (8)colors of eraser clay^pencil^clay shaping tool^(2)sheets of papercraft displays I had some low expectations after reading some of the reviews that people posted about this craft kit. Still the price was reasonable so I ordered one. This is not the first Klutz craft kit we've played with - so it was a familiar experience as those other kits. There really wasn't much in the box - the clay, a pencil (without an eraser), a sculpting tool, and a couple sheets of foldable paper props for the erasers you make (if you make the ones shown in the instructional guide).

You get plenty of different color clay - if you limit yourself to making fairly small erasers. The clay we got wasn't dried out - but it did take some kneeding to get soft enough to shape. Baking the erasers was simple - we used a toaster oven. Just be sure to use the right temperature and watch the erasers while they bake to make sure none start melting. Baking time can vary - mostly 15 to 30 minutes depending on the size & shape of the erasers you made.

The erasers are more ornamental than practical - but they do erase most pencil marks.

We're having fun with this kit - the instructional guide is outstanding. I'm happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: KLUTZ Make Your Own Mini Erasers Toy includes (8)colors of eraser clay^pencil^clay shaping tool^(2)sheets of papercraft displays
